meta.promptText: Which face wash should I buy for oily skin in India under ₹500?

response.text:
For **oily skin in India under ₹500**, I’d pick based on whether you also get pimples/blackheads:

### [The Derma Co Sali-Cinamide Anti-Acne Face Wash]()
*₹232*

### [Chemist At Play Oil & Acne Control Face Wash]()
*₹233.19*

### [Simple Kind to Skin Refreshing Facial Gel Wash]()
*₹204*

### [Plum Green Tea Pore Cleansing Face Wash]()
*₹149*

### [Fixderma Salyzap Face Cleanser]()
*₹234*

### My picks

**🥇 Best overall: The Derma Co 2% Salicylic Acid + 2% Niacinamide**  
Around **₹230–₹400**. Best if your oily skin also has **blackheads, clogged pores or occasional acne**. Salicylic acid is oil-soluble and helps clear pore congestion. [www.ndtvshopping.com](https://www.ndtvshopping.com/beauty-and-grooming/best-salicylic-acid-face-washes-for-acne-prone-skin-in-monsoon-11662605?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**🥈 Best if you're very oily/acne-prone: Fixderma Salyzap**  
Around **₹220–₹300**. A good option if controlling oil and breakouts is your priority. [www.ndtvshopping.com](https://www.ndtvshopping.com/beauty-and-grooming/best-salicylic-acid-face-washes-for-acne-prone-skin-in-monsoon-11662605?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**🥉 Best gentle everyday option: Simple Refreshing Facial Gel Wash**  
Around **₹200–₹260**. Choose this if you're oily but **don't have much acne** or if salicylic-acid cleansers tend to leave you dry/irritated.

**Also good: Plum Green Tea Pore Cleansing Face Wash**  
Currently around **₹150–₹350** depending on seller/size. A straightforward budget choice for oily skin. [www.vogue.in](https://www.vogue.in/content/best-cleansers-for-oily-acne-prone-skin-you-can-buy-for-under-rs-500?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### What I'd buy
If you tell me **“oily + acne” → The Derma Co 2% Salicylic Acid**.  
If **“just oily, no acne” → Simple Refreshing Facial Wash**.

You don't need an expensive ₹500 cleanser—the options above are comfortably within your budget. Also, don't assume a stronger/higher-percentage active is automatically better; formulation and how your skin tolerates it matter. Why more ingredients don't always mean better skincare
sources.snippet: The article "Why more ingredients don't always mean better skincare" from the Times of India (dated August 13, 2026) discusses the growing trend of ingredient-focused skincare shopping. Consumers increasingly recognize ingredients like niacinamide and salicylic acid and often rely on percentage values listed on product labels to judge the product's strength. However, the article emphasizes that higher concentrations or a longer ingredient list do not necessarily result in better skincare outcomes. Instead, it suggests that factors like ingredient synergy, formulation quality, and individual skin compatibility play a more crucial role in determining a product’s effectiveness.
